newsitem.title: JAPAN: NEC announces $1 billion China chip venture.
newsitem.headline: NEC announces $1 billion China chip venture.

text.p: Japan's biggest semiconductor maker, NEC Corp., formally signed an agreement with a Chinese partner Wednesday to set up a major chip manufacturing plant in Shanghai.
An NEC spokesman said the total cost of the joint venture, the latest sign of moves by Japanese electronic makers to move into the vast China market, would be $1 billion.
He said NEC and its Chinese partner, Shanghai Hua Hong, would design, manufacture and market semiconductors using NEC's latest chip technology.
NEC will contribute 28.6 percent of the venture's $700 million capital and Shanghai Hua Hong the remaining 71.4 percent. The plant will be based in Shanghai's Pudong district.
It will start full-scale production of dynamic random access memory chips (DRAM) and applied specific integrated circuits in the first half of 1999, he said.

The plant is expected to produce about 20,000 units of the 8-inch wafers a month, to be supplied primarily to the Chinese market, which is on a drive to modernise the country's information infrastructure and technology.
The spokesman said the agreement was a result of NEC's participation in China's five-year plan to develop its semiconductor industry.
It is the second big NEC investment in China following the setting up of a personal computer manufacturing plant, also in Shanghai, two years ago.
Masahiro Ono, an analyst at Credit Lyonnais Securities Japan, said the new plant was a gamble on China's manufacturing and technology future.
"It's a bit risky. It's hard to predict how far NEC could raise the production yields at the new China plant," Ono said. "It is an investment in the future."
